stories.summary: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NLAS Aftermath of a drone attack near the Ukrainian-Moldovan border Image: OdeskaODA/Telegram Advertisement Just a few months ago, Russia's war was an distant reality for many people in Europe outside of Ukraine. If Russian drones occasionally entered the airspace of countries like Poland or Romania, even official statements seemed strangely dismissive and abstract. Even after a Russian drone struck a high-rise apartment building in the eastern Romanian city of Galati in late May this year, many EU and NATO representatives hesitated to accuse Russia of intentional action. At most, there was discussion of hybrid warfare. The situation has changed radically since the summer. Drone overflights have become almost daily in certain parts of central and southeastern Europe, and there have even been crashes and explosions, particularly in countries bordering Ukraine. Alerts are becoming more frequent, with authorities increasingly having to close airspace or suspend operations at airports, as unauthorized flights are detected. stories.summary: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5N3KT Spangdahlem Air base is located in western Germany, near the Luxembourg border. Image: Harald Tittel/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement A fighter jet crashed near the US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany , on Tuesday. The plane crash occurred at approximately 2:30 p.m. local time (12:30 UTC). The cause of the incident is currently under investigation. The US military confirmed that the plane was an F-16 Fighting Falcon assigned to the 52nd Fighter Wing and that its pilot was able to safely eject from the aircraft. "The pilot ejected safely and is receiving medical care," the base said in a statement. At least one person was injured, authorities said Image: Harald Tittel/dpa/picture alliance Local authorities in the remote Eifel region also confirmed that one person had been injured. "Following a plane crash in the vicinity of US Air Base Spangdahlem, fire and emergency response teams from the Eifel District of Bitburg-Prüm were dispatched to the scene," the district said on its website. stories.title: How are Danes reacting to the US-Greenland security deal?
stories.summary: People in Copenhagen give mixed reactions to a new security deal between the US, Denmark and Greenland, with some welcoming closer Arctic cooperation while others say the agreement does little to ease their concerns.

stories.title: West Bank herders use donkeys and trenches to move milk at night
stories.summary: West Bank herders move milk by donkey through a deep trench at night, saying new access restrictions and lack of roads block routes to fields.

stories.title: Uzbekistan highlights Central Asia cooperation at UN General Assembly
stories.summary: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of Uzbekistan’s Presidential Administration, used her UN address to focus on regional cooperation, Afghanistan and reform of the organisation. She also covered domestic reforms, AI, human rights and environmental challenges.
